prime.options.header.high_risk: Prime: High-Risk Experiments (May Crash the Game)
prime.options.path_tracing.tooltip: Enables Prime path-traced rendering. Disable it to restore vanilla rendering when you need more performance or encounter compatibility problems.
prime.options.additional_specular_bounce: Sets the realtime delta-chain length (1–64, default 16): up to this many ideal specular reflection or transmission events are followed before the first non-delta surface.
prime.options.minimum_bounces.tooltip: Sets the minimum realtime path length (1–8, default 2). Internally this is the fixed no-roulette Wavefront prefix, including the primary-surface round, before the Megakernel Tail.
prime.options.maximum_bounces.tooltip: Sets the regular-transport bounce limit (1–64, default 16). Realtime counts the primary-inclusive fixed Wavefront prefix and Megakernel Tail, excluding the preceding delta chain; values below Minimum Bounces add no further limit. Offline uses this total directly.
Limits Prime terrain building to this percentage of Minecraft's maximum background workers. Lower values reduce competition with chunk loading but make Prime geometry appear more slowly; at least one worker is always used.
prime.options.material.surface_detail.to: Selects one texture-surface representation. Resource-pack normals use only normal textures supplied by the active pack and stay flat when absent; geometry displacement builds real relief from pack height data.
prime.options.material.displacement_heig: Adjusts texture-derived geometry height. 0% is flat, 100% is the default height, and higher values produce stronger relief; it applies only in Geometry Displacement mode.
prime.options.screenshot_mode.tooltip: Freezes the current scene and continuously accumulates samples so noise decreases over time. Press F2 once the image is ready; press Escape or Ctrl+Alt+F2 to exit. This mode lasts only for the current game session.
prime.options.post_processing.mode.toolt: Selects the realtime denoising and upscaling solution. DLSS RR requires a compatible NVIDIA RTX GPU and falls back to NRD + FSR when unavailable.
prime.options.post_processing.quality.to: Controls the internal path-tracing resolution. Quality presets preserve more detail at a higher cost, while performance presets usually improve frame rate; start with Performance and raise it when frame rate allows.
prime.options.post_processing.rr_respons: Submits a uniform signed responsivity mask to DLSS RR in the API range [-1, 1]. The default is -0.25. This setting lasts for the current session only.
prime.options.astronomy.latitude.tooltip: Controls the sun's altitude, day length, and orientation of the night sky. Set it to the geographic latitude you want to simulate; northern and southern latitudes have opposite seasons.
prime.options.astronomy.season.tooltip: Sets the sun's position through the year, changing its altitude and the length of the day. 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270° are the March equinox, June solstice, September equinox, and December solstice; it does not advance with game time.
prime.options.lighting.sun_ev.tooltip: Adjusts sunlight, the sky, and the atmosphere together. Adding 1 EV approximately doubles their brightness; use it when the whole outdoor scene looks too bright or too dark.
prime.options.lighting.star_ev.tooltip: Adjusts the night sky and the illumination it produces. Adding 1 EV approximately doubles brightness; use it when the night sky looks too bright or too dark.
prime.options.lighting.block_light_ev.to: Adjusts illumination from emissive blocks such as torches and glowstone. Adding 1 EV approximately doubles brightness without changing which blocks emit light.
prime.options.lighting.transparent_nee_m: Stable Filtering accumulates transparent-medium absorption along the original shadow line and is steadier at finite sample counts. Path Sampling stops shadow lines at smooth transparent interfaces, so transmitted direct light comes only from random paths and needs many samples. Neither mode solves refracted shadow connections.
prime.options.display.auto_exposure_comp: Controls how strongly exposure adapts to scene brightness. 0% uses a fixed baseline and 100% follows automatic metering fully; lower it if brightness changes are too noticeable.
Adjusts the brightness of the final image. Positive values brighten it and negative values darken it; use this first when the entire image looks too bright or too dark.
prime.options.display.reference_white.to: Sets the HDR brightness of SDR white in nits. Automatic uses the Windows value for the active display; manual values are limited to that display's HDR peak. This calibrates physical brightness without changing the SDR Reinhard-Gamut curve.
prime.options.display.hdr.tooltip: Extends Reinhard-Gamut highlights to the active display's HDR headroom and presents linear scRGB. scRGB 1.0 represents 80 nits; Prime scales both the world and UI to the calibrated reference white.
prime.options.display.hdr.unavailable.to: No usable HDR output is available on the current screen. Make sure the display supports HDR and Windows HDR is enabled.
prime.options.material.default_roughness: Applies to materials without a PBR roughness value. Lower values look smoother with clearer reflections; higher values produce softer highlights. It does not override roughness supplied by a resource pack.
prime.options.material.seamless_glass.to: Makes glass borders and interiors use the same smooth transparent material, reducing block seams and frosted areas. Disable it to restore the borders and surface variation authored by the resource pack.
prime.options.material.air_gap.tooltip: Adds a sub-pixel air sheet between different solid transparent materials with matching IOR, preserving a cut reflection. Water, incompatible roughness, and unequal-IOR contacts keep their direct medium boundary.
prime.options.material.vanilla_pbr_prese: Applies conservative defaults to homogeneous vanilla materials that have no authored PBR parameters. Per-texture resource-pack parameters always take precedence.
prime.options.debug.renderer_diagnostics: Shows runtime information such as resolution, geometry counts, and exposure. Enable it when troubleshooting performance or preparing a bug report; it lasts only for the current game session.
prime.options.debug.raw_output.tooltip: Displays the current raw path-traced frame at native resolution without denoising or image reconstruction. This session-only control is intended for diagnosing noise and sampling problems.
prime.options.debug.renderer_image.toolt: Shows a renderer output full-screen or in an unstretched square grid whose first cell is always the denoised output.
prime.options.debug.rr_input.tooltip: Shows the exact inputs submitted to DLSS Ray Reconstruction full-screen or in a square grid.
prime.options.debug.nrd_input.tooltip: Shows the unmodified input images submitted to both REBLUR instances and SIGMA full-screen or in separate square grids.
prime.options.low_latency.reflex_mode.to: Paces frame simulation through Streamline's Reflex driver to reduce input-to-photon latency. On + Boost additionally keeps GPU clocks high. When a framerate limit is set, Reflex takes over frame pacing from the vanilla limiter.
prime.options.low_latency.reflex_mode.un: Requires Windows, an NVIDIA GPU, and a successful Streamline initialization.
prime.options.streamline.dlss_frame_gene: High-risk experiment. NVIDIA Streamline/DLSS-G currently has a Vulkan synchronization defect that Prime cannot work around; enabling it may immediately crash with VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST. Use for testing only. It will not be treated as a regular feature until NVIDIA fixes the defect. Requires Windows, a compatible NVIDIA GPU, Streamline, and Reflex.
Sets the output-frame multiplier for each rendered frame. The available maximum is determined by the driver and Streamline.
Separates the game's UI opacity for DLSS-G recomposition. Requires DLSS Frame Generation and a compatible Streamline UI alpha path.
